title: cdp-smoke-ci-binary-fetch-pattern
desc: cdp-smoke CI fails when core-* releases share identical createdAt timestamp: sort-by-createdAt is non-deterministic, and the bin cache skip condition can serve a stale binary. Canonical fix: gh release download --latest + no if-condition.
steps: ROOT CAUSE A (2026-06-28): Two core-* releases with IDENTICAL createdAt -- the PowerShell Sort-Object createdAt -Descending picks non-deterministically. Sometimes CI gets the fix binary, sometimes not. Diagnosis: gh release list --json tagName,createdAt,isLatest.@@ROOT CAUSE B: Fetch step has 'if: hashFiles(bin/wkappbot-core.exe) == empty' -- bin cache restores old binary so the Fetch step is SKIPPED entirely. CI runs with stale binary permanently.@@FIX in cdp-smoke.yml: (1) Remove the 'if:' condition line from Fetch step. (2) Replace the 8-line PowerShell sort/select/download block with one line: gh release download --latest --repo env:CORE_REPO --pattern wkappbot-core.exe --dir bin --clobber.@@IMMEDIATE TRIAGE (no yml edit needed): delete the ambiguous release without the fix -- gh release delete TAGNAME --repo kiexpert/WKAppBot --yes. This leaves only the correct Latest release for the sort to find.@@ALWAYS-VERIFY release timestamps when CI binary behavior is flaky: gh release list --repo REPO --json tagName,createdAt,isLatest -- identical createdAt = non-deterministic.@@INCIDENT DATE: 2026-06-28. Releases involved: core-ci-headless-20260626 (with fix, isLatest=true) vs core-20260625-2219-7dbba19 (without fix, same createdAt). Deleted the latter as immediate fix.
